source.title: Frozen Memory Is Not Enough: Rethinking External Memory as Extraction
source.authors: Ming-Yuan Li; Guang-Sheng Yu; Xu Wang; Shao-Xiong Ji

record.tranche_reason: The study measures cross-model representational similarity with linear CKA, a different measure from directly testing convergence as models scale. It does not test whether similarity rises with scale or capability.
record.gate_note: Only the Appendix C.5 CKA measurements bear on representational alignment. The many memory-transfer, perplexity, and QA results test frozen-memory extraction, not the claim versions. The CKA analysis does not measure a scale trend, cross-modal alignment, or metric/data sensitivity.
record.test_reason: Appendix C.5 is a small diagnostic, not a convergence study. It measures linear CKA between mean-pooled layer ⌊L/3⌋ representations of three independently trained LMs on WikiText-103. Its own numbers bear on how incomplete cross-model alignment is. It gives one snapshot with no scale or capability sweep, so it bears on V7 only. The memory-transfer, perplexity and QA results test portability of an external memory artifact, not representational convergence.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors state that representational similarity alone does not predict the size of transfer gains. They attribute transfer utility to the target reader's ability to recover and route information from the frozen memory.
record.recipe_differences: Uses linear CKA at one intermediate layer on WikiText-103 to compare three model pairs; it does not test a convergence-with-scale or performance sweep. The paper cites the Platonic Representation Hypothesis but does not reproduce its central scaling test.
record.method_sensitivity: not tested for the CKA analysis: only one similarity measure, one selected depth, and WikiText-103 inputs are reported.

fits_no_version.finding: A frozen memory table trained with Pythia-160M improves TinyLlama perplexity by 10.6% through a small linear-gated reader. This holds even though their hidden-state CKA is near zero (0.013); the high-CKA Pythia pair gains only 1.6%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Usability of one model's learned artifacts by another does not track measured representational similarity (CKA).

record.problems: The claim-relevant CKA evidence covers only three model pairs, one intermediate depth, and WikiText-103. No uncertainty estimate is reported for the CKA values, and the analysis does not vary model capability, similarity measure, layer, or input distribution.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were left out. The paper's other reported results concern memory transfer and downstream task performance rather than the claim versions.

untested.parts: No scale or capability trend; only three small models (160M–1.1B) in one snapshot.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation test between model representations; the reader maps memory vectors, not hidden states.
Only one measure (linear CKA), one layer, mean pooling and one dataset; no variation.

Plateau not tested. Whether shared data or objectives explain alignment is not tested: the higher Pythia–Pythia CKA fits shared training data, but it is confounded with shared architecture, tokenizer and stage.

record.verdict_notes: The study cites the Platonic Representation Hypothesis only as motivation for a linear reader. The CKA evidence is thin: three pairs, one depth, mean pooling, no uncertainty and no null baseline. The TinyLlama checkpoint is chat-tuned, which adds a confound to the cross-family comparison. The C.5 text says WikiText-103 is used 'for training', but the CKA computation is an evaluation-only pass over shared input sequences.

versions.untested_parts: Whether alignment increases with model size or capability across independently trained models.
Vision-language alignment on paired images and captions, and its relationship to model capability.
Convergence across random seeds of the same architecture, including shared features or subspaces.
Whether model representations can be mapped, stitched, or transferred by the methods named in this version.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
Whether convergence changes across similarity measures, metric settings, or input distributions.
Whether alignment plateaus; whether shared training data or objectives explain it; and whether these findings generalize beyond the three compared models, the selected layer, and WikiText-103.

rows.subject: Pythia-160M ↔ Pythia-410M
rows.operation_detail: Compared mean-pooled hidden representations using linear CKA.

conditions.value: approximately one third depth: block 4 of 12 for Pythia-160M and block 8 of 24 for Pythia-410M

rows.note: Representations were mean-pooled over non-padding tokens. This pair had greater similarity than either pair involving TinyLlama, but the value is below the self-similarity diagonal of 1.000.
rows.check: CKA 0.595 is clearly below complete alignment, even for a same-family, same-tokenizer, same-training-data pair. 'Partial' misreads the state: the V7 effect (incomplete alignment) is present. No chance-level or null CKA baseline is given.

relationships.condition: Pythia-160M, Pythia-410M and TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat; linear CKA on mean-pooled layer ⌊L/3⌋ states over WikiText-103
relationships.reason: Cross-model CKA is well below 1: 0.595 within the Pythia family (R1) and near zero across families, 0.013 and 0.007 (R2, R3). Alignment is far from complete in this setting. The study has no null baseline and does not vary measure or layer.
relationships.display_finding: CKA was 0.595 within Pythia but only 0.013 and 0.007 across families, without a null baseline or comparisons across measures or layers.

relation.reason: Appendix C.5 directly measures cross-model representational alignment, providing results on the incomplete-alignment component of V7.

tranche.reason: The external-memory transfer setting includes an original intermediate-representation diagnostic bearing on incomplete alignment. It does not systematically investigate convergence with scale.

source_check.notes: The diagnostic uses one layer per model and one corpus, with no null baseline or reported CKA uncertainty. It establishes neither a scale trend nor causes of alignment; the authors conclude that backbone similarity alone does not predict frozen-memory transfer gains.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: The three model pairs measured at approximately one-third depth on WikiText-103
reader_labels.reason: The measured CKA values are below the self-similarity value of 1.000, and the two cross-family comparisons are especially low (R1–R3); this is evidence of incomplete pairwise representational alignment in these settings, not evidence about why it occurs.
